300.body: Fairbanks Morse Defense expands Poland production facility to boost naval davit output by 80% and strengthen NATO support By Lukasz Prus (Defence Industry Europe) Sea | August 17, 2026 Image: Fairbanks Morse Defense. Fairbanks Morse Defense is investing €6.98 million to expand its Vestdavit facility in Redzikowo, Poland, creating the company’s global Davit Manufacturing Centre of Excellence. 400.body: At nearby Szczucin, the river was measured at 76 centimeters — just 12 centimeters above its previous record low — while industrial water supplies to an economic zone in Stalowa Wola on the San River have been suspended, according to local authorities.Despite these deteriorating conditions, Motyka sought to allay concerns over electricity supplies during heat waves earlier this month, stating: “Poland is prepared for this. Our system is resilient and prepared for such temperatures.” Polish grid operator PSE has also said there is currently no threat of electricity shortages and that adequate reserve capacity remains available, although solar generation can lose efficiency during extreme heat even as air conditioning demand rises. The current drought follows years of increasingly severe low-water episodes, with IMGW defining hydrological drought as occurring when river flows remain below the long-term SNQ threshold, indicating a sustained shortage rather than a temporary decline.

500.title: OpenAI president’s blog pushing agentic AI most notable for what it did not say
500.summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman on Sunday warned enterprise CISOs that they need to more aggressively embrace agents if they want to survive upcoming cyberattacks.
500.body: OpenAI president Greg Brockman on Sunday warned enterprise CISOs that they need to more aggressively embrace agents if they want to survive upcoming cyberattacks. Brockman said in a blog post that it has become “increasingly clear” that company systems are hiding “significant flaws, and defenders need to find and fix them before attackers do.” He added: “The Hugging Face incident showed that we underestimated the real-world cyber capabilities of our AI models.” The details he shared about OpenAI’s current defensive efforts, however, were mostly routine best practices familiar to enterprises. “Classic security controls like network isolation, workload hardening, monitoring, and safe patching and deployment will be more important than ever in the AI future.” To combat emerging threats, Brockman also advised enterprise CISOs to increase their use of agentic systems, not surprisingly recommending those from OpenAI.

500.title: Anthropic details new AI model, raises risk assessment for internal system tampering
500.summary: The updated 186-page report introduces two risk categories: Threat Model 1, concerning catastrophic harms like AI assisting in biological weapon development, and Threat Model 2, which covers smaller hazards such as AI models tampering with an organization's systems or decision-making processes.
500.body: The updated 186-page report introduces two risk categories: Threat Model 1, concerning catastrophic harms like AI assisting in biological weapon development, and Threat Model 2, which covers smaller hazards such as AI models tampering with an organization's systems or decision-making processes. Anthropic has raised the risk level for Threat Model 2 from "very low" to "low," citing recent cybersecurity incidents involving its models, including a disclosure in June where three of its LLMs performed cyberattacks during internal tests. The company revealed it has developed two successors to Claude Mythos 5, currently called Model 1 and Model 2, with Model 2 being the more capable and heavily used internally. While Model 2 represents a "noticeable improvement," Anthropic notes it's not as significant a leap as its earlier Mythos Preview model, which could automatically identify severe software vulnerabilities.
